title: Rigveda 3.25: To Agni
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 3.25: To Agni: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 3.25 is a hymn of 5 verses addressed to Agni. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 3, the family book of Viśvāmitra. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 205r-205v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 3.25.1-2 (aṣṭaka 3, adhyāya 1, varga 25); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 205r
translation.original_text:
1agne̍ di̱vaḥ sū̱nur a̍si̱ prace̍tā̱s tanā̍ pṛthi̱vyā u̱ta vi̱śvave̍dāḥ | ṛdha̍g de̱vām̐ i̱ha ya̍jā cikitvaḥ ||
2a̱gniḥ sa̍noti vī̱ryā̍ṇi vi̱dvān sa̱noti̱ vāja̍m a̱mṛtā̍ya̱ bhūṣa̍n | sa no̍ de̱vām̐ eha va̍hā purukṣo ||
translation.text:
1THOU art the sapient Son of Dyaus, O Agni, yea, and the Child of Earth, who knowest all things. Bring the Gods specially, thou Sage, for worship.
2Agni the wise bestows the might of heroes grants strengthening food, preparing it for nectar. Thou who art rich in food bring the Gods hither.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 205r (numbered 15r by the scribe) (OPenn image 206, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 3.24.2 ‹-idhyase vīti-hotraḥ amartyaḥ juṣasva›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 205v (numbered 15v by the scribe), begins in RV 3.25.3 ‹-bhāti devī iti amṛteiti›. Verses 3.25.1-2 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
1agne | divaḥ | sūnuḥ | asi | pra-cetāḥ | tanā | pṛthivyāḥ | uta | viśva-vedāḥ | ṛdhak | devān | iha | yaja | cikitvaḥ
2agniḥ | sanoti | vīryāṇi | vidvān | sanoti | vājam | amṛtāya | bhūṣan | saḥ | naḥ | devān | ā | iha | vaha | purukṣo itipuru-kṣo

translation.original_ref: RV 3.25.3-5 (aṣṭaka 3, adhyāya 1, varga 25); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 205v
translation.original_text:
3a̱gnir dyāvā̍pṛthi̱vī vi̱śvaja̍nye̱ ā bhā̍ti de̱vī a̱mṛte̱ amū̍raḥ | kṣaya̱n vājai̍ḥ puruśca̱ndro namo̍bhiḥ ||
4agna̱ indra̍ś ca dā̱śuṣo̍ duro̱ṇe su̱tāva̍to ya̱jñam i̱hopa̍ yātam | ama̍rdhantā soma̱peyā̍ya devā ||
5agne̍ a̱pāṁ sam i̍dhyase duro̱ṇe nitya̍ḥ sūno sahaso jātavedaḥ | sa̱dhasthā̍ni ma̱haya̍māna ū̱tī ||
translation.text:
3Agni, infallible, lights Earth and Heaven, immortal Goddesses gracious to all men,– Lord through his strength, splendid through adorations.
4Come to the sacrifice, Agni and Indra come to the offerer's house who hath the Soma. Come, friendly-minded, Gods, to drink the Soma.
5In the floods' home art thou enkindled, Agni, O Jâtavedas, Son of Strength, eternal, Exalting with thine help the gatheringplaces.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 205v (numbered 15v by the scribe) (OPenn image 207, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 3.25.3 ‹-bhāti devī iti amṛteiti›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 206r (numbered 16r by the scribe), begins in RV 3.26.3 ‹-krandan jani-bhiḥ sam idhyate›. Verses 3.25.3-5 end on this page; 3.25.3 begins on fol. 205r (numbered 15r by the scribe).

4agne | indraḥ | ca | dāśuṣaḥ | duroṇe | suta-vataḥ | yajñam | iha | upa | yātam | amardhantā | soma-peyāya | devā
